findings.title: The request context can cancel the asynchronous legacy write
findings.body: The timeout context inherits the incoming request context, so it does not keep the legacy write alive after the request completes. HTTP servers cancel request contexts when handlers return; because these methods return immediately after starting the goroutine, the legacy operation can be canceled before it finishes. The 10-second timeout only limits a live parent context and cannot extend a canceled one, so mode 3 may routinely fail to mirror writes. Use a context that preserves needed values but is detached from request cancellation before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Concurrent writes can reach legacy storage out of order
findings.body: Each successful mutation starts an independent goroutine, with no ordering or per-object serialization. For example, a create followed quickly by a delete can have the legacy delete run first and the delayed create run afterward, leaving a deleted object in legacy storage; successive updates can likewise let an older update overwrite a newer one. This breaks the dual-write consistency the mode is intended to provide and can make legacy API results stale. Preserve mutation order when dispatching legacy writes.

findings.title: Storage failures are recorded as legacy failures
findings.body: This branch handles a failed unified-storage create, but records it with `recordLegacyDuration` and the storage-operation start time. The storage failure is therefore attributed to legacy metrics, while the storage metric is not updated; the update failure branch has the same mistake at line 129. Record these failures against storage so operators can correctly diagnose which backend is failing.

findings.title: Delete metrics use the object name as the kind label
findings.body: The successful delete path passes `name` to `recordStorageDuration` where other paths pass `options.Kind`. If this argument is used as the metric kind label, every distinct deleted object name creates a separate time series instead of grouping by resource kind, causing unbounded metric cardinality and misleading metrics. Pass the resource kind here.

findings.title: Legacy delete-collection latency is recorded as storage latency
findings.body: This goroutine measures the legacy `DeleteCollection` call but reports it through `recordStorageDuration`. As a result, legacy latency and failures are attributed to unified storage, and the legacy metrics omit this operation. Record the result through `recordLegacyDuration`.
